name: Bateham's yard: kindling wood and furniture lumber

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: Standing on the night of the fire, which destroyed it (Andreas vol. 2, pp. 406, 712-718).

change_note: Built T-3831 (2026-11-28): drawn in the 1871 scene on the landmark_1871 archetype, in place of the generic context fill that stood on its lot.

placement.position_note: In the mills' yard (Andreas vol. 2, pp. 713, 717); the piles are set along the Canal Street front and north of the mills, the lumber between the mills (reconstructed). The footprint's origin is local E -157.1 N -1531.0.
placement.symbolic_location: Canal Street south of Harrison, in front of and north of Bateham's mills.

footprint.note: The ground between the main mill and Canal Street, and the north yard; their bounds are reconstructed inside Andreas's acre and a half.

fire.note: 'At half-past ten, the heroic men were driven from Bateham's works by the intense heat' (Andreas vol. 2, p. 717); 'At 10:30 Bateham's mills on Canal Street, near Harrison, were deserted, as beyond salvation' (p. 719). Bateham: 'The materials from this mill will fire the South Side, and nothing can prevent it now.'

research_note: BATEHAM'S YARD, built by T-3831 for the 1871 scene: on the night of the fire Bateham and his watchman 'flooded everything in the yard, in which were a thousand cords of fire-kindling wood, in piles twenty-five feet high, and also six hundred thousand feet of furniture lumber ... Near by were seven hundred and fifty thousand shingles. The grounds occupied by these mills comprised one and a half acres' (Andreas vol. 2, p. 717). Foreman Swenie of No. 14 'placed one line of hose in the yard' (p. 713). Where in the grounds the piles stood is not recorded.
